chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man whose wife had taken khula' (divorce by redemption) from him: Is it permissible for him to propose marriage to her sister before the waiting period of the woman who took khula' has expired? He said, 'Yes, her bond of marriage has been severed from him and he has no right of return over her.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever divorces a young girl who has not yet reached menstruation, and he has already consummated the marriage with her, her waiting period is three months if she is of the age at which women menstruate, which is nine years; and if she is younger than that, there is no waiting period for her due to divorce.

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He consummated the marriage with her

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a pre-pubescent girl divorced after consummation, and can her ex-husband marry her sister during this time?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that in *khula'* (divorce by redemption), the wife's bond is severed immediately, allowing her sister to be married before the *iddah* concludes, distinguishing it from revocable divorces. It further specifies the *iddah* for pre-pubescent girls as three months if they have reached the age of nine, aligning with the majority Shia view, while exempting those younger than nine from any waiting period.
